response.answer: The context does not record any test or observation confirming that a minted token was actually verified to work on only one app. What is recorded is the design/implementation: `mintDeployToken` in packages/control-plane/src/fly.js calls Fly's `createLimitedAccessToken` GraphQL mutation with `profile: 'deploy'` and `profileParams: { app_id: flyApp }` plus `expiry: '1h0m0s'` (packages/control-plane/src/fly.js:48-56), and decision d2 states the intent was to scope the token to exactly one app and expire it in 1 hour, motivated by the concern that 'any authenticated user gets credentials for every machine in the org' (m1812). Decision d7 also notes a correction that the mutation required `app_id` rather than `app_name` in profileParams (m2077), which was necessary for the scoping to work as intended — but this is a fix to the request shape, not a reported verification that the resulting token was actually restricted at use-time. No session message or decision cites an observed test (e.g., attempting to deploy a second app with the token and having it rejected) confirming the scope held. Next step: if scope enforcement needs confirming, run a check where a minted token is used against a different `app_id` and the failure is logged as an observation.

messages.text:
Move the Fly deploy out of the CLI and into the control plane. Today /api/deploy returns the org-wide Fly token and the CLI runs flyctl with it — any authenticated user gets credentials for every machine in the org. That must end before a second user exists.

New flow: the CLI packages the app directory into a tarball and POSTs it to /api/deploy with small.toml and secrets. The Worker holds FLY_API_TOKEN as a secret and does everything itself via the Fly Machines API: create the Fly app if missing, trigger a remote build from the tarball, create or update the machine with the image, secrets, and SMALL_PROXY_SECRET, allocate a shared IPv4 on first deploy, and store the origin in D1. The CLI never sees a Fly token, never shells out to flyctl, and never contains anything Fly-specific. Remove the flyctl dependency from packages/cli entirely.

If a remote build from a tarball via the Machines API is not workable, fall back to: the Worker mints a scoped Fly deploy token limited to that one app, expiring in one hour, and returns that to the CLI instead of the org token. Document which path you took and why.

Keep the integration test passing: deploy examples/counter end to end, confirm the fly.dev origin still 403s, and add an assertion that the CLI's config file and network traffic contain no Fly token. then update v1 and v2 if needed

Big one. Plan:

1. Spike: verify Fly GraphQL `createLimitedAccessToken` (scoped 1h deploy token) + Machines API app create actually work from plain HTTPS — decides primary vs fallback
2. Worker: create Fly app + allocate IP + mint scoped token itself; stop returning org token
3. CLI 0.0.4: drop `apps create` (worker does it), publish
4. Tests: counter e2e + 403 + no-token assertions + scoped-token-can't-touch-other-apps
5. Docs v1/v2 updates, commit, push

Up front on the primary path: Fly has no REST "build from tarball" endpoint — remote builds speak the Docker/BuildKit wire protocol to a builder machine, which a Worker can't (no raw TCP, no docker client). So the scoped-token fallback is the workable route; spike will confirm. Verifying now:

All code is ready and green (CLI 10/10, worker rewired, tests written). **Blocked on you now** — everything left needs the org admin token:

1. Go to https://fly.io/dashboard/personal/tokens
2. Create token → type **Admin** (org-wide, not app-scoped) — this is what lets the worker mint the 1h per-app tokens
3. Replace the `FLY_API_TOKEN=...` line in `.env` with it (current one is stale anyway — it can't even manage machines)

Then say "done" and I'll: verify mint works with it → set worker secret + deploy worker → publish CLI 0.0.4 → run the full integration suite (counter e2e, fly.dev 403, no-token-leak, scoped-token-401-on-other-app) → update docs v1/v2 → commit and push.

What's staged, for the record:
- Worker `/api/deploy` and `/api/logs` no longer return the org token — worker creates the Fly app, allocates the shared IPv4, and mints a **1h deploy token scoped to that one app** via Fly's GraphQL `createLimitedAccessToken`. Fails closed (502) if minting fails.
- CLI 0.0.4: `flyctl apps create` removed (worker owns it). flyctl remains for build/deploy per the sanctioned fallback — Fly has no tarball-build REST API; remote builds need the Docker/BuildKit protocol a Worker can't speak. Will document exactly this.
- New tests: config + stdout must contain no `FlyV1`/`fm2_`; the returned token must list its own app's machines (200) and get rejected (401/403) on another app's.

If it can't, plan B (guaranteed to work): in your own terminal run

```
~\.fly\bin\flyctl.exe auth login
~\.fly\bin\flyctl.exe auth token
```

and paste that token into `.env` instead — that's your full user token, which definitely can mint. Either way the token only ever lives in `.env` and the worker secret.

Confirmed: dashboard org tokens can't mint scoped tokens either — Fly only allows `createLimitedAccessToken` from your **user auth token**. Plan B, in your own terminal (not through me — it needs a browser):

```
~\.fly\bin\flyctl.exe auth login
~\.fly\bin\flyctl.exe auth token
```

Paste the output of the second command into `.env` as the `FLY_API_TOKEN=` value, then tell me. That token stays worker-side only; the CLI still ends up with nothing but 1h single-app tokens.

(Side note: your new token created a separate org `small-deploy` — existing apps live in `personal`, and the user token covers both, so I'll keep deploys in `personal`. No migration needed.)
Spike passes — mint works, own app 200, other app **403**. Wiring it all up:

Done — shipped and live, pushed as `f9026a7`. Full suite **9/9 in 84s** including a real counter deploy through the new flow.

**Path taken: the documented fallback — worker-minted scoped tokens.** The primary path (CLI tarball → worker builds via Machines API) is not workable: Fly has no build-from-tarball REST endpoint; remote builds speak the Docker/BuildKit wire protocol to a builder machine, which a Cloudflare Worker can't. Verified empirically before committing to the fallback.

**What changed:**
- Worker (`src/fly.js`): creates the Fly app (`POST /v1/apps`), allocates the shared IPv4 (idempotent GraphQL mutation), and mints a **deploy token scoped to exactly one app, expiring in 1 hour** (`createLimitedAccessToken`, `profileParams.app_id`). `/api/deploy` and `/api/logs` return only that. Fails closed with 502 if minting breaks. Org-wide credentials never leave the worker.
- CLI **0.0.4** published: `flyctl apps create` removed; keeps flyctl only for build+deploy with the throwaway token, per the fallback.
- Tests added and passing: `~/.small/config.json` and deploy stdout contain no `FlyV1`/`fm2_`; the returned token lists its own app's machines (200) but gets **403** on another app's; fly.dev origin still 403s; counter e2e green.

**Credential findings** (cost us two round-trips, now documented): only your **user auth token** can mint limited tokens — both dashboard org tokens returned UNAUTHORIZED on `createLimitedAccessToken`. That token lives in `.env` and the worker secret only. Also: the mutation wants `app_id`, not `app_name`.

Docs updated: v1 ceilings struck through with supersession notes, v2 got an addendum with the full story. Note the worker redeploy also took the cold-start retry live. Loose ends for you: old CLI ≤0.0.3 installs break against the new worker (`npm i -g small-deploy` fixes), and the empty `small-deploy` Fly org from the token attempt can be deleted in the dashboard.

response.answer: The session's spike report (m2004) states the mint test passed with the specific check: requesting machines under the token's own app returned 200, while requesting another app's machines with the same token returned 403 — i.e. an empirical access-control test, not just inspection of the token's scope field. The final summary (m2077) repeats this as a shipped test: the returned token 'lists its own app's machines (200) but gets 403 on another app's.' This is an agent-reported test result, not independently verified in this context. Code-side, the scoping mechanism itself is the `profileParams: { app_id: flyApp }` argument passed to Fly's `createLimitedAccessToken` mutation in packages/control-plane/src/fly.js (lines 48-56), which is what the 200/403 behavior was checked against.

There is no separate 'session report' or test-run log in this snapshot showing the token being verified in practice. The only recorded evidence is the code and its accompanying comment in control-plane/src/fly.js. The comment states: "The only Fly credential the CLI ever sees: deploy-scoped to one app, dead in 1h" (line 48), and the mintDeployToken function backs this up by requesting a Fly GraphQL `createLimitedAccessToken` with `profile: 'deploy'`, `profileParams: { app_id: flyApp }` (scoping it to the single app being deployed) and `expiry: '1h0m0s'` (lines 49-55). This is the builder's recorded design intent and the shape of the API call — it documents that the token is meant to be single-app-scoped and short-lived, but the snapshot doesn't include an actual observation/log confirming that flyctl or Fly's API enforced that scope at runtime. If you need proof it actually behaves that way, the next step would be to inspect a real `tokenHeader` payload or attempt an out-of-scope Fly API call with it and confirm rejection.
